prompt_en: One stone golem in front of an old castle gate stands still. Its broad stone feet meet the worn flagstones and its heavy limbs remain close to the torso. The rough rock surface has distinct edges around the knees and shoulders. Soft cloudy light reveals the stone texture while the dark gateway provides separation behind its outline. The frame gives the golem's stone body priority against the old gate. The photograph shows the quiet aftermath of a constructed-material golem performing one task, with the single figure now motionless. The stationary figure has one complete body assembled from nonliving stone, with its head, chest, arms and broad feet reading as a single agent. The same stone continues across torso, limbs and joints, with uninterrupted rough surfaces joining the chest, elbows, knees and ankles. Fitted stone blocks reveal deliberate construction through close seams at the shoulders and hips of the motionless figure. Dust and shifted grit around the grounded feet preserve traces of earlier independent movement; the golem itself stands still at this shutter moment. The opened passage records the completed task at the existing castle gate, leaving a clear route behind the resting stone figure.
